questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan(9x)}{7x}$$?

options.why: $$\frac{\tan u}{u} \to 1$$ only when the angle and the denominator match. Here they differ by a factor of $$\frac{9}{7}$$.

Correct. Write it as $$\frac{9}{7} \cdot \frac{\tan(9x)}{9x}$$; the second factor approaches 1.

questions.explanation: Using $$\lim_{u \to 0} \frac{\tan u}{u} = 1$$ with $$u = 9x$$: $$\frac{\tan(9x)}{7x} = \frac{9}{7} \cdot \frac{\tan(9x)}{9x} \to \frac{9}{7}$$.

questions.stem: If $$\int_0^{4} f(x)\,dx = 6$$ and $$\int_0^{8} f(x)\,dx = 1$$, what is $$\int_{4}^{8} \left(4f(x) - 3\right)dx$$?

options.why: This adds the two given integrals; the integral from a to b is their difference.

questions.stem: A population $$P$$ grows according to $$\frac{dP}{dt} = kP$$, and it doubles every 7 years. If $$P(0) = 1000$$, what is $$P(14)$$?

questions.stem: A farmer has 232 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

questions.stem: What is the total area of the regions enclosed by the graphs of $$y = x^3$$ and $$y = x$$?

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$c$$, for $$3 < c < 9$$, such that $$P'(c) = 0$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Mean Value Theorem (or Rolle's Theorem) with its conditions.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is differentiable (so continuous), and $$P(3) = P(9) = 53$$. By the Mean Value Theorem there is a $$c$$ with $$P'(c) = \frac{53 - 53}{6} = 0$$.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$t$$, for $$0 < t < 3$$, at which $$P(t) = 51$$? Justify your answer.
